House of Student Raises $2M Seed  

House of Student Raises $2M Seed

House of Student, a San Francisco, California-based provider of a global student living technology platform and housing marketplace, has raised $2M in Seed funding. The capital includes a mix of equity and debt, intended to support the company's growth as it manages a vast network of student accommodations worldwide.

## Investors [...] ## Investors

The funding round was co-led by Saltwater Sutra and Nirmitsu Inspirational Ventures. Additional participating investors included Gautam Verlekar, Glen Fernandes, Richard McCallum, Ali Moosa, and existing investors from Unilodgers.

## House of Student Use of Funds

The company plans to use the newly raised capital to accelerate product innovation, enhance its AI-driven capabilities, and drive global expansion efforts.

# House of Student raises $2M seed to grow AI-driven student housing platform

House of Student raises $2M seed to grow AI-driven student housing platform

What's the deal? Student accommodation platform House of Student has raised $2 million in seed funding, co-led by Saltwater Sutra and Nirmitsu Ventures. The round combined equity and debt.

Who's backing it? Participants include Gautam Verlekar, Bank of New York Mellon managing director Glen Fernandes, former UK India Business Council chief executive Richard McCallum, and Singapore Gulf Bank executive vice-chairman Ali Moosa. Existing investors from Unilodgers also joined. [...] By the numbers: Headquartered in San Francisco with teams across India, the UK, and the Middle East, the company says it runs the world's largest student housing supply network — more than 2.5 million verified rooms across 25-plus countries, including the US, UK, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UAE, and Singapore.

The signal: At $2 million, this is a modest seed even by early-stage standards, landing in the bottom third of comparable rounds. But the founder's prior marketplace experience and an existing global supply network give House of Student a running start as it bets on AI to reshape student services.

Read more: entrepreneur.economictimes.indiatimes.com

Image credit: Peter Alfred Hess

75

Get AI-powered insights [...] What's the endgame? Founded by Vaibhav Verma, the company builds on Unilodgers, the student housing marketplace he previously founded. It plans to evolve beyond accommodation into a broader technology platform supporting students through higher education.

In Verma's words: “We want to become the world's most trusted company around student life.”

Where the money goes: House of Student will use the capital to accelerate product innovation, expand housing supply, strengthen AI capabilities, and support international expansion.
